subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Three-Phase Power: Smooth Rotation
description: A quick, practical guide to Three-Phase Power: Smooth Rotation.

hook.text: A single-phase motor needs a trick to start. Three-phase motors start themselves.

buildup.text: Three coils spaced 120° apart produce a smoothly rotating magnetic field.

discovery.text: The rotating field provides constant torque — no pulsation like single-phase.

twist.text: Swap any two phases and the motor reverses — the rotating field flips direction.

climax.text: Factories worldwide use three-phase power because motors run smoother and more efficiently.

punchline.text: Three phases, 120° apart — the smoothest way to spin a magnetic field.

quiz.question: How do you reverse a three-phase motor?
options: Reduce the supply voltage by half
Swap any two of the three phase connections
Add a capacitor to one of the phases
